Selling guide

What's worth fixing before you list

Buyers have more choice than they did a few years ago, so condition matters. Here's where your money goes furthest.

Ali Bayat
Figures checked against the sources below on November 21, 2026
Published November 21, 2026
3-minute readFor sellersUpdated November 2026
The short version
  • Fix anything an inspector would flag: leaks, broken fixtures, missing alarms.
  • Clean, declutter, paint and light. These cost the least and change photos the most.
  • Skip full renovations. You rarely get the cost back, and they delay your launch.

01Why condition matters right now

4.6Months of inventory, GTAOctober 2026, trend; buyers have options
31 daysAverage days on marketGTA, October 2026
97%Sold price vs. list priceGTA average, October 2026

02Fix, maybe, skip

Fix

Things buyers and inspectors will find

  • Leaks, drips and water stains
  • Broken windows, doors, locks and fixtures
  • Working smoke and carbon monoxide alarms
  • Burnt-out bulbs and loose outlet covers

Maybe

Worth it if the gap is obvious in photos

  • Fresh neutral paint in busy rooms
  • Worn carpet in one main room
  • Dated light fixtures and cabinet hardware
  • Front door, porch and garden tidy-up

Skip

Rarely pays back before a sale

  • Full kitchen or bathroom renovation
  • High-end custom finishes
  • Finishing a basement just to sell
  • Big landscaping projects

03A four-week prep plan

  1. 01

    Walk-through and list

    Week 1

    Walk the home with your agent, make a fix list and get quotes. Consider a pre-listing inspection ($350–$600) so nothing surprises you on offer night.

  2. 02

    Repairs

    Week 2

    Book trades for the fix list. Use a written contract for any job over $50.

  3. 03

    Declutter and paint

    Week 3

    Pack a third of what's in each room. Paint, deep clean, swap bulbs to one colour temperature.

  4. 04

    Photos and launch

    Week 4

    Final clean, staging touches, professional photos, floor plan, then go live.

04Paperwork buyers will ask for

  • Permits for past workAdditions, basements, decks and structural changes.
  • Rental equipmentWater heater, furnace or AC rental contracts and buy-out amounts.
  • Utility costsA year of heating, hydro and water bills.
  • Upgrades with datesRoof, windows, furnace and AC, with receipts or warranties.
Ali's take

Spend on what shows up in photos and what an inspector would write down. Everything else is a negotiation you can handle on offer day.
